findings: All six hook-only profiles reproduce prior native move, completed depth, node count and white score. No production search/evaluator mutation.
The Ng5-preroot position spends 9999 of 10000 nodes in quiescence even with threats disabled. Stop is node budget, not the unresolved-check 32-ply safety ceiling. Maximum qply is 19 OFF and 22 ON.

ON: 7705 qnodes go to Qe1; seven distinct root moves visited, Ng5 root branch not reached. OFF: Re1 5261 and Qe1 3307 qnodes; 13 root branches visited. This is root-move starvation under a finite shared budget, not a searched recommendation for fxg7 fallback.

ON: 2138 checked qnodes (21.38 percent of qnodes); 2494 repeated full-history/budget/ply qstates (24.94 percent), of which 1671 repeats share alpha/beta. Captures, promotion/recapture chains and checks re-encounter equal states after irreversible moves reset repetition context.

There is no q transposition lookup in the archived production implementation. The normal TT is bypassed at depth zero before quiescence. A separate budget/history aware q bound cache can potentially avoid recomputation while keeping the candidate set and all check evasions/threat defenses.

A q cache must distinguish position key, repetition context, halfmove counter, remaining qply, check/threat budgets, defensive-reply mode and mate ply; retain valid lower/exact/upper bounds and legal complete PV; store only completed calls. Normal-depth and q entries must never alias.

Duplicate fractions are diagnostic opportunities, not measurements of actual cache savings. They include terminal/static leaves; table replacement and bound-window compatibility reduce use. The unvisited tail of the first iteration is unknown, so completing within 10000 nodes is not guaranteed.
